docs.title: Why Now
docs.text:

  4. Remote/hybrid work — Distributed teams need digital-first HR, not office-based HR departments.
  5. No one is building a complete AI HR department — Competitors build point solutions (a chatbot, a recruiting tool). No one is delivering a full HR function with 18 virtual employees across 5 divisions.

docs.title: The Agent Factory Division
docs.text:
One of the five divisions in our AI HR department. When a company needs to fill any role, the Agent Factory analyzes the job description and decides: human or agent?

  1. A company submits a job description (any role — secretary, financial analyst, market researcher, HR coordinator, etc.)
  2. The Agent Factory analyzes the role — tasks, skills, judgment required, human interaction level
  3. It decides: Can an AI agent do this job? Fully? Partially? Or does it require a human?
  4. If an agent can do it: Deploy a virtual employee with a name, role, KPIs, and communication channels
  5. If it needs a human: Route to the Recruitment Operations Agent in HR Shared Services to find the right person

docs.title: Core Beliefs
docs.text:
1. HR is essential but broken — Most companies either can't afford a full HR function or suffer from inconsistent, outdated HR practices.
  2. Not every job needs a human — Many knowledge-work roles are process-heavy and rule-based. AI agents can do them better, cheaper, and 24/7.
  3. AI can deliver consistent excellence — Unlike human teams that vary in quality, AI agents deliver best-practice execution every single time.
  4. The future of work is hybrid: humans + agents — Companies will have org charts with both human and virtual employees. We build the platform that makes this possible.
  5. People operations should be proactive, not reactive — AI enables a shift from firefighting to strategic workforce planning.
  6. Compliance shouldn't require an army of lawyers — AI agents can stay current with regulations across jurisdictions automatically.
  7. Every employee deserves a great HR experience — Regardless of their employer's size or budget.

docs.title: For Small & Mid-Size Companies (10–500 employees)
docs.text:
• Can't afford a full HR team — A competent CHRO costs $150K–$300K+/year. An HR team of 3–5 people costs $400K–$800K/year.
  • Rely on ad-hoc HR — Founders, office managers, or finance leads "do HR on the side," leading to compliance gaps, poor hiring, and employee dissatisfaction.
  • Use fragmented tools — Cobble together 5–10 SaaS tools (ATS, payroll, benefits, LMS) with no integration or strategic layer on top.
  • Reactive, not proactive — Only deal with HR when something goes wrong (lawsuits, turnover spikes, failed audits).

docs.title: For Large Companies (500+ employees)
docs.text:
• HR is expensive and slow — Typical HR-to-employee ratio is 1:100. A 2,000-person company has 20 HR staff.
  • Inconsistent quality — HR depends on individual competence. Some HR business partners are excellent; others are not.
  • Buried in administrative work — 60–70% of HR time goes to transactional tasks (paperwork, queries, compliance tracking) rather than strategic work.
  • Compliance risk — Especially for multi-country operations, keeping up with labor laws is a full-time job.

docs.title: For Employees (the end user)
docs.text:
• Poor HR experience — Slow responses, unclear policies, inconsistent treatment.
  • No 24/7 support — HR operates on business hours; employee needs don't.
  • Lack of transparency — Employees don't know their rights, benefits, or growth paths because HR doesn't communicate proactively.

docs.title: The Root Cause
docs.text: HR is a knowledge-intensive, process-heavy, regulation-bound function that has been underinvested in technology. Current HR tech automates workflows (e.g., applicant tracking, payroll processing) but doesn't automate judgment, strategy, or expertise — which is where AI agents come in.

docs.title: The Opportunity
docs.text:
AI agents can now: - Understand and apply complex labor regulations - Make consistent, bias-reduced decisions - Operate 24/7 across time zones and languages - Learn and improve from every interaction - Scale from 10 to 10,000 employees with near-zero marginal cost

This is the first time in history that the full HR function can be delivered as a service through software.

docs.text: The global Human Resource Management (HRM) market encompasses all software, services, and outsourcing related to managing people within organizations.

docs.title: What the Agent Factory Does
docs.text:
The Agent Factory is the workforce composition division within HR. When a company needs to fill a role, the Agent Factory analyzes the job description and decides: should this role be a human or a virtual employee? If an agent can do the job, the factory deploys one. If not, it routes the role to recruiting.

This is a new HR function that doesn't exist in traditional organizations — it's what makes an AI HR department fundamentally different.

docs.title: How It Works
docs.text:
INPUT: Job Description (any role the company wants to fill)
  ↓
STEP 1: Parse the JD into structured components
  - Core responsibilities and daily tasks
  - Required skills and judgment level
  - Human interaction requirements (internal, external, sensitive)
  - Decision-making authority
  - Creative vs. process-driven work ratio
  - Regulatory/legal implications
  ↓
STEP 2: Score each dimension on an "AI Readiness" scale
  - Task repeatability:        [Low ←──→ High]
  - Rule-based vs. judgment:   [Judgment ←──→ Rule-based]
  - Human empathy required:    [High ←──→ Low]
  - Data availability:         [Low ←──→ High]
  - Error tolerance:           [Zero ←──→ Flexible]
  - Compliance sensitivity:    [High ←──→ Low]
  ↓
STEP 3: Generate recommendation
  - 🟢 FULL AGENT: AI agent can do 90%+ of this role → Deploy virtual employee
  - 🟡 HYBRID: AI agent can handle 50-90% → Deploy agent + human oversight
  - 🔴 HUMAN NEEDED: Role requires >50% human judgment → Route to Recruitment Ops
  ↓
STEP 4: Configure and deploy (if agent)
  - Create virtual employee profile (name, role, team, KPIs)
  - Connect to relevant systems and communication channels
  - Set escalation rules and human oversight parameters
  - Deploy to the customer's workspace

Agent Factory (decided human vs. agent)

docs.title: Journey 1: Company Onboarding (Admin sets up the platform)
docs.text:
Day 0: Admin signs up → selects company size, industry, locations
  ↓
Day 0: Upload existing policies, handbook, org chart (or let AI generate from scratch)
  ↓
Day 0: Connect integrations (Google Workspace / M365, Slack, payroll system)
  ↓
Day 0: Import employee directory (CSV or HRIS sync)
  ↓
Day 1: Compliance Agent audits uploaded policies → flags gaps → suggests fixes
  ↓
Day 1: Admin reviews and approves AI-generated policies
  ↓
Day 2: Employee Relations Agent goes live — employees get Slack/email intro
  ↓
Week 1: First analytics report generated for admin

docs.title: Journey 2: Employee Asks a Question
docs.text:
Employee sends message via Slack: "How many vacation days do I have left?"
  ↓
Employee Relations Agent checks employee profile → PTO balance
  ↓
Agent responds: "Hi Sarah, you have 12 vacation days remaining this year.
  You've used 8 days so far. Would you like to request time off?"
  ↓
Employee: "Yes, I'd like to take Dec 20-24 off"
  ↓
Agent checks: team calendar, blackout dates, manager approval rules
  ↓
Agent: "I've submitted your request for Dec 20-24 (3 business days).
  Your manager Ahmed will be notified. I'll let you know once approved."
  ↓
Agent sends approval request to manager Ahmed via Slack
  ↓
Ahmed approves → Agent confirms to Sarah → Calendar updated

docs.title: Journey 3: Hiring a New Employee (End-to-End)
docs.text:
Manager submits hiring request: "I need a Senior Product Designer"
  ↓
Recruitment Agent generates job description based on role level + company context
  ↓
Manager reviews and approves JD (with edits)
  ↓
Agent posts to LinkedIn, Indeed, company careers page
  ↓
Applications come in → Agent screens and ranks top 10 candidates
  ↓
Agent presents shortlist to manager with match scores and key highlights
  ↓
Manager selects 5 for interviews → Agent schedules with interview panel
  ↓
Agent sends interview guides and scorecards to interviewers
  ↓
Post-interview: Agent collects feedback, generates summary, recommends top pick
  ↓
Manager decides → Agent generates offer letter using compensation bands
  ↓
Offer accepted → HANDOFF to Onboarding Agent
  ↓
Onboarding Agent activates: welcome email, document collection, IT setup,
  orientation schedule, buddy assignment, 30/60/90 plan

docs.title: Journey 4: Compliance Alert
docs.text:
Labor law changes in [jurisdiction] → Compliance Agent detects update
  ↓
Agent analyzes impact on company's current policies
  ↓
Agent generates: "Alert: New overtime regulations in California effective March 1.
  Your current overtime policy needs 2 updates. Here's what changed and
  my recommended policy language."
  ↓
Admin reviews → approves changes → policies auto-updated
  ↓
Agent notifies affected employees and managers of policy change
  ↓
Agent schedules mandatory training if required

docs.title: Journey 5: Employee Offboarding
docs.text:
Manager initiates: "Alex is leaving. Last day is Feb 28."
  ↓
Offboarding Agent activates → generates customized checklist
  ↓
Agent schedules exit interview with Alex (AI-conducted)
  ↓
Agent coordinates: IT access revocation, equipment return, final pay calc
  ↓
Agent generates separation documents for Alex to sign
  ↓
Agent processes: PTO payout, benefits continuation info (COBRA)
  ↓
Exit interview completed → insights added to attrition analytics
  ↓
Agent sends alumni welcome and references Alex's manager for future requests

  • Easy to understand and compare
  • Predictable for customers

docs.title: Agent Design Principles
docs.text:
1. Each agent is autonomous — Can handle its domain end-to-end
  2. Agents collaborate — Share data and hand off tasks to each other
  3. Human-in-the-loop — Configurable escalation rules per company
  4. Auditable — Every decision and action is logged
  5. Configurable — Companies can customize agent behavior without code

docs.title: 1. Router (Intent Detection)
docs.text:
• Receives user message from any channel
  • Classifies intent (e.g., "leave request" → Employee Relations Agent)
  • Handles multi-turn conversations
  • Routes to the appropriate agent

docs.title: 2. Agent Runtime
docs.text: Each agent has: - System prompt — Role definition, company context, behavioral rules - Tools — Functions it can call (database queries, API calls, send emails) - Memory — Conversation history + long-term context - Guardrails — What it can and cannot do - Escalation rules — When to involve a human

docs.title: 3. Action Engine
docs.text:
• Executes real-world actions on behalf of agents
  • Examples: send email, update calendar, create document, update database
  • All actions are logged and reversible where possible
  • Approval workflows for sensitive actions

docs.title: 4. LLM Gateway
docs.text:
• Abstracts LLM provider (swap models without changing agent code)
  • Routes to appropriate model based on task complexity
  • Handles rate limiting, retries, fallbacks
  • Tracks token usage and costs

docs.title: Recommendation
docs.text: Start with LangGraph or Anthropic Agent SDK for MVP. Build custom orchestration layer on top. Avoid over-engineering — simple prompt + tools pattern works for most agents initially.

docs.title: Model Selection Criteria
docs.text:
1. Reasoning quality — HR decisions require nuanced judgment
  2. Instruction following — Agents must follow company policies precisely
  3. Safety & alignment — Cannot give harmful advice on employment matters
  4. Cost efficiency — Must keep COGS low for healthy margins
  5. Speed — Employee-facing agents need fast response times
  6. Privacy — Employee data must not be used for model training
  7. Multi-language — English first, Arabic and others later

docs.text: Task Type Model Rationale Simple Q&A (policies, PTO balance) Small/fast model (Claude Haiku, GPT-4o-mini) High volume, low cost Complex reasoning (compliance analysis, conflict resolution) Large model (Claude Opus, GPT-4) Accuracy critical Document generation (handbooks, offer letters) Mid model (Claude Sonnet, GPT-4o) Balance of quality and cost Classification/routing Fine-tuned small model or embeddings Speed and cost Data extraction (resume parsing, document processing) Specialized model or mid-tier Structured output

docs.title: Why Multi-Model?
docs.text:
• 80% of queries can be handled by cheaper, faster models
  • Only 20% need expensive large models
  • Reduces average cost per query by 60–70%
  • Improves response time for simple queries

docs.title: RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation) Architecture
docs.text:
Each agent needs access to company-specific knowledge:

Employee Question → Query Understanding → Retrieve Relevant Context → Generate Answer

Context Sources:
├── Company policies & handbook
├── Employee data (profile, PTO, comp)
├── Labor laws (by jurisdiction)
├── Previous interactions & decisions
├── Industry best practices
└── Company-specific configurations

docs.title: Why Security is Critical
docs.text: HR data is among the most sensitive data a company holds — salaries, SSNs, health information, disciplinary records. A breach would be catastrophic for trust and the business.

docs.title: Security Principles
docs.text:
1. Zero trust architecture — Verify everything, trust nothing
  2. Encryption everywhere — At rest, in transit, in processing
  3. Least privilege — Agents and users only access what they need
  4. Audit everything — Every action is logged and traceable
  5. Privacy by design — Data minimization, purpose limitation

docs.title: Data Encryption
docs.text: Data State Method In transit TLS 1.3 At rest AES-256 PII fields Application-level encryption (per-tenant keys) Backups Encrypted

docs.title: Authentication & Authorization
docs.text:
• SSO/SAML for Enterprise customers
  • MFA required for all admin accounts
  • Role-based access control (RBAC)
  • API keys with scoping and rotation
  • Session management with timeouts

docs.title: AI-Specific Security
docs.text:
• No training on customer data — LLM providers must not use our data for training
  • Prompt injection protection — Input sanitization and guardrails
  • Output filtering — Prevent agents from leaking cross-tenant data
  • Hallucination guards — Agents must cite sources for compliance answers
  • Human escalation — Sensitive decisions always involve humans

docs.title: Infrastructure Security
docs.text:
• VPC isolation
  • WAF (Web Application Firewall)

docs.title: AI in Employment — Legal Risks & Considerations
1. AI Bias in Hiring
docs.text:
• AI screening tools can discriminate based on protected characteristics

docs.text:

  • EU AI Act classifies HR AI as "high risk" — requires conformity assessment

docs.text:

docs.title: 4. Employee Monitoring / Privacy
docs.text:

  • Must be transparent about what data is collected and how it's used
  • Mitigation: Clear privacy notices, data minimization

docs.title: 5. Worker Classification
docs.text:

  • Mitigation: Clear that we are a tool provider, not an employer

docs.title: The Problem
docs.text: Most companies either can't afford a proper HR function or are burdened by an expensive, inconsistent, and reactive HR department. docs.text: [Company Name] is an AI-native HR company that deploys a suite of specialized AI agents to handle the full scope of HR operations — recruitment, onboarding, compliance, employee relations, performance management, payroll, and more. Companies subscribe to our platform instead of building or outsourcing an HR department.

docs.text: Companies connect our platform to their existing tools (Slack, email, calendar). Our AI agents understand their policies, org structure, and local labor laws. Employees interact with agents naturally for any HR need. Admins get a real-time dashboard with compliance status, workforce analytics, and agent performance metrics.
